Bialy Baker's Percentage

Divide this batch into 10 small rounds of 79.3 g. Press a well in the center, fill it with chopped onion, and bake. Do not boil them.

Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 56% hydration, 1.8% salt, and 0.8% yeast. That is 280 g water, 9 g salt, and 4 g yeast, 793 g of dough. The balls fields open at 10 pieces of 79.3 g. Press a well in each small round and fill it with chopped onion. Do not boil them. Onion and poppy seed are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 280 g water, 9 g salt, and 4 g instant yeast, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and firm. At 56% the dough feels stiff. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 80 minutes. With 0.8% yeast it should grow by about half.
  3. Divide Divide the 793 g dough into 10 pieces of 79.3 g, the weight in the balls fields. Roll each into a smooth round, cover, and rest 10 minutes.
  4. Well Press a thumb into the center of each round and flatten that middle so it stays lower than the rim. Leave a well, not a hole. Do not boil these rounds.
  5. Fill Put about 8 g of finely chopped onion in each well. A pinch of poppy seed on the onion is traditional. Both are extra and are not in the gram total. The photo shows the onion in the well.
  6. Proof Cover the rounds for 20 to 30 minutes, until they look slightly puffy. Skip any boil.
  7. Bake Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Bake 12 to 16 minutes, until the rim is golden and the onion is cooked. The center stays flatter than the rim.
